4. It appears that land measuring 1.90 acres recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 528 appertaining to Touzi No. 314 is the subject matter of the suit for khas possession. Plaintiff claimed it on the basis of his auction purchase of the Touzi in revenue sale held on 27-9-50 which was confirmed on 27.11.50 and delivery of possession given on 7.4.51. Thereafter all the under tenures appertaining to the said Touzi were annulled in a regular proceeding; and the plaintiff got possession of all lands excepting the suit land. According to the plaintiff he has already possession of .43 acres of land of the said khatian which has been described in schedule "Ka". The suit land has been described in schedule "Kha", to the plaint. C. S. Khatian No. 528 is directly under C.S. KhatianNo. 527 which records the tenure right of the predecessor of the plaintiff. Keramaullah Talukder, father of the plaintiff settled the disputed land with (1) Rabiullah and Yeadullah, (2) Keramatullah, (3) Banari Bibi, and (4) Sonaullah by 4 pattas dated 3.12.27. According to the defendant the pattas created a mokararijote right but according to the Plaintiff it created an under tenure holding. 

 11. The above noted recitals show that the lessee was allowed to hold the land at fixed rate of rent; and it authorized the lessee to collect rent by setting up tenants on the land. The pattas land was recorded in C S. Khatian No. 528 as “মধ্যস্বত্ব চিরস্থায়ী স্বত্বের”…… With reference to the terms in the pattas the lower Appellate Court held that defendant is a tenure bolder. According to him, since the inception of the tenancy shows in clear terms that the defendant took settlement of the land with the right of a tenure-holder and not with a raiyati right. Thus it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge confined his consideration on the question of nature of the tenancy merely with reference to recitals of the patta but without any consideration as to the nature of use of the land by the lessee since its inception. The plaintiff in this suit prayed for khas possession of 1 90 acres of land recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 528 on the basic of his auction purchase in revenue sale of Touzi No. 314 of Bogra Collectorate. According to the plaintiff’s case, he has already got possession of.43 acres or land of the same khatian, but due to obstruction he did not succeed in taking possession of 1.90 acres of land of the said khatian. Defendant No.1 gave a total denial about the annulment of the encumbrance and their knowledge about the said proceeding with regard to .43 acres in the possession of the plaintiff. His case is that the plaintiff's father Keramatullah Talukder took khas possession of it as putnidar in Title Suit No. 171 of 1947 of the Munsif, First Court, Bogra. According to the defendant, plaintiff never took possession of it. The defendant's further case is that plaintiff's father settled the disputed land with (1) Rabiullah and Yadullah; (2) Karamatullah Talukder, (3) Banari Bibi, and (4) Sonaullah by 4 pattas dated 3-12-1927 in makarrarijote right, and on the same day they made a wakf by a registered deed of wakf and the defendant became the mutwalli. The mere fact that a person has acquired from a proprietor or from another tenure-holder a right to hold land for the purpose of collecting rent is not sufficient to prove that he is a tenure-holder. It must be proved on evidence that since the inception of the tenancy land was let out for agricultural or horticultural purpose. This principle, as it appears from the judgment of the lower Appellate Court and that of the High Court Division, was not followed in determining the controversy between the parties on the question of nature of the tenancy created by the pattas Exhibit D series dated 3.12.1927. 

 12. The defendant's specific case is that by the patta a raiyati with occupancy right was created and not a tenure as claimed by the plaintiff, and this gets support from the use of the land by the defendant from the very inception of the tenancy. The defendant led the evidence to prove that the land has been under direct cultivation of the defendant. Defendant filed certain dakhilas Exhibit. A to A(5) of which Exhibit A is in the hand-writing of the plaintiff and Exhibits A to A( 5) are in the hand writing of Keramatullah Mondal, plaintiff's father. C.S. Khatian No. 528 is included in all these dakhilas except A(2) and A(3). With reference to these dakhilas the learned Munsif rightly observed that it no longer lies in the mouth of the plaintiff to say that defendants are "Niskar tenure-holder as recorded in khatian and not raiyati." The defendant also filed a decree made in Title Suit No. 171 of 1947 (Exhibit E) which shows that the suit was brought by Keramatullah Mondal on the basis or auction purchase of schedule "Ka" land in rent sale. The decree also belies the statement of the plaintiff that he got possession of schedule 'Ka' land on the basis of revenue sale and got possession through the Collectorate. With reference to the above mentioned materials the learned Munsif correctly arrived at the finding that by the pattas raiyati with occupancy right was created, and the suit land does not appertain to an under-tenure holding as claimed by the plaintiff. By the pattas dated 3-12-1927 a tenancy in the nature of makarrari jote right was created and the interest thus acquired by the defendant is protected from annulment under section 37 of the Revenue sale law. In this context it may be mentioned that the recitals in the pattas lend considerable support to the defendant's case that “স্বাধীন প্রজালিলি” was not the dominant purpose of creation of the tenancy by the pattas Exhibit D series.
